title: Null pointers
recap: nullptr expresses the absence of an address. Testing a pointer checks whether it is null; testing the pointed-to integer checks an entirely different thing.
A non-null check is necessary before indirection but does not prove that an arbitrary pointer is otherwise valid. These tests supply either live objects or nullptr.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement valueOr(value,fallback), returning the pointed-to integer when value is non-null, otherwise fallback. Do not dereference a null pointer. The pointee is read-only through this pointer.
hints: Check the pointer itself before reading *value.
A pointer to integer zero is still non-null.
